html:
Timgad is a Roman town in the Aurès mountains of northeast Algeria, founded by the emperor Trajan around 100 CE as a colony for army veterans.

It was laid out on a perfect grid of streets, with a forum, a theatre, libraries, baths and a triumphal arch, and later grew beyond its walls. It shows Roman town planning more clearly than almost any other site. It flourished on the farms of Numidia, and later became a centre of the Donatist church.

The town declined after the Vandal and Byzantine periods and was abandoned after the Arab conquest. Sand covered it until excavation began in 1881. It became a World Heritage Site in 1982. See also Roman Africa and El Jem.
sum: Timgad is a Roman town in the Aurès mountains of northeast Algeria, founded by the emperor Trajan around 100 CE as a colony for army veterans.
